recommendation: Retain the reviewed ROWS expression path and RANGE public-collector runtime for this fix. A later unified runtime should establish mixed-function memory and latency acceptance first.
feasibility: TCoreWinFramesCollector::CreateFactory already accepts RowIntervals and RangeIntervals in the same public object.
TFrameBoundsIndices exposes GetIntervalInQueueByRow with the same queue-relative half-open bounds as GetIntervalInQueueByRange.
A frame-kind flag could select the interval without changing the absolute-index/deque algorithm; ROWS validation would accept a single row interval and permit absent sort order.
The existing deserialize and ConvertBoundsToComparators path handles ROWS and preserves current clipping/unbounded semantics.

estimated_footprint.estimated_net_reduction_lines: approximately 115–140, before implementing and reviewing the exact diff

memory.current_rows: One established WinFramesCollector row buffer plus aggregate-specific two-stack entries containing ordinal, value and cumulative extremum.
memory.unified_minmax_only: One caller-owned row buffer plus candidate deques, bypassing the second collector. This is plausibly smaller but has not been measured.
memory.unified_mixed: Adds a caller-owned row buffer before the existing collector and output row copies, while replacing stack entries with smaller/pruned candidate entries. The net change depends on row width, number of MIN/MAX fields and data order.
memory.adverse_case: Wide rows with few MIN/MAX fields and broad following windows can add nearly another full window/partition of retained row arrays. Candidate pruning cannot bound this row storage.
memory.latency: Following bounds would require future prepass output before the outer collector advances, potentially doubling finite following lookahead. Unbounded-following still requires a partition drain.
memory.measurements: None; all statements are source-derived storage obligations.

alternatives.runtime_only_for_minmax_only: Avoids mixed ROWS extra buffering but keeps the ROWS stack implementation, losing most code reduction and adding another lowering choice.
alternatives.share_existing_outer_queue: WinFrame consumes its established private queue resource; reusing that representation violates the public-interface constraint. A new public frame/list bridge would broaden this change.
alternatives.runtime_handles_all_functions: Would move COUNT/SUM/AVG/native semantics into a new runtime implementation and exceeds the narrow MIN/MAX correction.

source_references.reason: Existing expression path accesses its established private queue resource.
The stream wrapper owns its queue; only all-admitted-MIN/MAX windows bypass the second collector.
Current ROWS aggregates consume the original collector frame and retain scalar stack entries.
